newsitem.title: UK: London freight - Firmer rates still elude owners.
newsitem.headline: London freight - Firmer rates still elude owners.

text.p: A widespread view in the freight market this week that nearby weakness in the Atlantic would be soon be succeeded by firmer conditions has not yet been fulfilled, brokers said.

On the contrary lower rates have been reported in the US Gulf/Far East Panamax trades and some brokers now describe this market as having "gone off the boil" and as "wobbly" - one grain charterer's broker believed "we have seen the best of it for while". Coal trading in the Atlantic is especially quiet and Caper rates generally are flat. The BFI was down 2 points to 1458.

With little business quoted for Panamaxes from US Gulf to the Far East it was no surprise to brokers that President G 69,344 dwt was reported fixed by Samsun delivery 6/12 March on this route at a weaker $15,000 daily plus $285,000 bonus (some estimated the rates at $14,800 daily plus $280,000). Also down was Pan Ocean's reported fixture of 54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan for 15/27 March at $24.75 no combo - 50 cents off - although again there were alternative versions of this rate circulating at $24.50 and $24.90 no combo.

News of Nidera's fixture of 65,000 corn US Gulf/Lisbon for 1/15 March at $11.75 was discounted by grain brokers. Iranian charterers Atlantic Shipping fixed the 1978-built Amber 67,812 dwt delivery Hansaport 7/12 March for 3-5 months redelivery Continent at a net figure of $9,250 daily. Much has been made of the potential of Argentinian grain to push the market up but so far only rumours of fixtures have surfaced. Finagrain may have covered a couple of Panamaxes in this area for 2 laden legs Atlantic trading, Transcatalana are said to have fixed a Panamax for Plate/Spanish Med, and Shipmair are believed to have relet Mare Baltico 64,310 dwt open spot Plate for business to the Continent, but full details are lacking.

Smaller sizes featured reports that Dreyfus may have booked the 1974-built Vernal Spirit 2.3m cft for about 35,000 grains US Gulf/Spanish Med at a lumpsum of $465,000, although some thought the charterers could have a Lisbon option on this vessel. Sometra were linked with Akmi 28,000 dwt for a prompt timecharter trip from N France to W Africa, possibly at about $5,750 daily. Few new orders were seen but they included Halla with 54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan for April and May (ideas said to be $25.00 no combo) and Nidera with 20,000 grains 57' Plate/Continent-Denmark for 10/15 march.

One owner's broker admitted that despite a fair volume of chartering enquiry rates have not reacted positively'. British Steel chartered tonnage for 80,000/10 coal Mobile and Hampton Roads to Port Talbot at a modest $8.25 basis 2-1. Exemplar 122,000 open Ireland mid-march was fixed for unknown business, and rumours that Nafsika M 162,000 dwt was fixed from the Continent for Saldanha Bay ironore to China at $8.00 could not be confirmed. Docenave were lied with Corriente 158,000 dwt delivery Japan end March for 2 laden legs via Vancouver and Brazil, but full details were not available. Docerio 167,315 dwt was said to have failed on subjects with Trend Power for Brazil/China ironore business.

Combac fixed Calypso n 34,000 dwt delivery prompt Continent for a trip to US Gulf at close to $6,500 daily. Angelia P 23,000 dwt was understood booked by Sealift delivery prompt Continent trip E Africa in the region of $7,000 daily. Fednav took a 22,000 dwt vessel spot E Canada for a trip to the Continent on private terms. Brokers reported very difficult conditions for Handies under 25,000 dwt in the Far East.
